chunks: Yunus narrated from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), that among the treasures preserved is the completion of prayer in the two Sanctuaries.

key_terms.الْإِتْمَامَ: Completion; performing an act fully with all its required components and recitations.
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries; specifically referring to Masjid al-Haram in Mecca and Masjid al-Nabawi in Medina.
key_terms.الْمَذْخُورِ: Treasure or preserved wealth; something of lasting value stored up.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of praying completely in the two holy sanctuaries according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) identifies the completion of prayer (*itmam*) within the two holiest sanctuaries as a form of 'stored treasure' (*al-madkhur*), emphasizing that the spiritual capital accumulated here is preserved for the Hereafter. This highlights the unique ontological status of Mecca and Medina in Shia jurisprudence, where the quality of worship is magnified by the sanctity of the location, turning routine acts into enduring assets.
